The phrase "Show me the man and I’ll show you the crime" is an infamous boast attributed to Lavrentiy Beria, the ruthless secret police chief under Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin.

The Meaning
It describes the exact opposite of the rule of law. Instead of investigating a crime to find out who committed it, this philosophy implies targeting a specific person first—usually a political rival or dissident—and then fabricating or finding any excuse to convict them.
